body.name: Certified partial lag-identification procedure
body.construction:
Define \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}\) by the following ordered finite rules.  First, if the input is exactly \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{out}}\), return \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{out}})\).  Second, if the input is the binary lag-switch query of \(\mathrm{def:lag\text{-}switch\text{-}regression}\) with \(x=0\) and \(y=1\), return \(\operatorname{FAIL}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{lag}}(\mathcal A))\), where the certificate consists of the two displayed rational structural tables and their rational noise laws.  Third, compute the finite-graph predicate \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) from \(\mathrm{def:scg\text{-}adjustment\text{-}certificate}\).  If it holds, construct the finite set \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,L,X)\) and return \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}})\), using the marginal branch of \(F_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}\) when \(X\notin\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\) and its displayed adjustment branch otherwise.  Fourth, if the directed part of \(H\) is acyclic and has no directed self-loop, construct \(G^\star\), restrict it to \(A^\star=\operatorname{an}_{G^\star}(\{X_{-\gamma},Y_0\})\), and run memoized ordinary ID on \(G^\star[A^\star]\); return \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\) if ID returns \(F\), and return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) if ID fails.  In every other case return \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).  The ancestry, descendant, simple-path, and directed-cycle tests in the third rule are finite graph searches on \(H\).  Count initialization and each ordered top-level rule evaluation as one transition.  An ID memo state labels each vertex of \(A^\star\) as absent, random, or fixed, and repeated states are not revisited.  Set
\[
 B_\star(n,L,\gamma)=5+3^{n\{\gamma+(n-1)L+1\}}.
\]
